bead.title: Specify postgres commit-transition parity scope (backend flavor, tables)
bead.description:
PROBLEM
pqueue-postgres ships two backend flavors: PostgresBackend (log-replay, crates/pqueue-postgres/src/lib.rs) and PostgresRelationalBackend (DB-authoritative, crates/pqueue-postgres/src/relational.rs). Both currently no-op CommitTransitionPort. It is not yet decided in writing which flavor(s) Snorri's Lakebase production deployment actually needs commit-transition parity on, or what the side-record/instance-fence table schema should look like on postgres (sqlite-relational's schema, added under epic pqueue-2201fd37, is the reference implementation).

PROPOSED FIX
Write a short decision doc (or an addendum to docs/helix/04-build/DEPLOYMENT-READINESS.md) settling: (a) which backend flavor(s) this epic covers -- relational only, log-replay only, or both, referencing which flavor Lakebase/Snorri production actually runs (see docs/helix/04-build/DEPLOYMENT-READINESS.md and ADR-008); (b) the postgres table schema for side records and instance fences, mirroring sqlite-relational's approach; (c) whether request-id retained-idempotency reuses an existing postgres idempotency mechanism or needs a new table.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- docs/helix/04-build/DEPLOYMENT-READINESS.md or a new docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/ note.

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Any code changes.
bead.acceptance:
1. `rg -n 'commit-transition|CommitTransitionPort' docs/helix/04-build/DEPLOYMENT-READINESS.md docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/` finds the new decision text naming exactly which postgres backend flavor(s) are in scope.
2. `cargo fmt --check` passes (no code touched).
